column3: NASB renders “seek” as “keep seeking” and reorders the verse.
NASB adds “that are.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB reads “our life,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “your life.” “Appear” is rendered “be revealed.”
NASB follows the critical text without “your”; it renders “put to death the members” as “consider the members of your earthly body as dead to,” “covetousness” as “greed,” and “is” as “amounts to.”
NASB has no “upon the sons of disobedience,” following manuscripts that lack it; “is coming” is rendered “will come.”
NASB follows the critical text (“them”).
NASB renders “rage” as “wrath” and “foul language” as “abusive speech.”
NASB adds “since” and “evil,” and renders “old man” as “old self.”
NASB adds “self” and renders “in knowledge” as “to a true knowledge.”
NASB adds “a renewal in which there is no distinction between” and introduces the verse with a dash.
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “the elect of God” as “those who have been chosen of God” and “hearts of compassion” as “a heart of compassion.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Lord”); “has forgiven” is rendered “forgave,” and it adds “should you.”
NASB follows the critical text (“which”); “bond of perfect unity” is rendered “perfect bond of unity.”
NASB follows the critical text (“of Christ”); it adds “indeed.”
NASB follows the critical text; “grace” is rendered “thankfulness,” and “yourselves” is “one another.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “do” and reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text without “own”; “was fitting” is rendered “is fitting.”
NASB renders “be harsh” as “be embittered.”
NASB follows the critical text; “pleasing in the Lord” is rendered “well-pleasing to the Lord.”
NASB renders “provoke” as “exasperate” and “become discouraged” as “lose heart.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “according to flesh” as “on earth” and “eye-service” as “external service,” and adds “merely.”
NASB follows the critical text; “from the soul” is rendered “heartily.”
NASB follows the critical text without “for”; it adds “It is … whom.”
NASB follows the critical text (“For”); “will be repaid” is rendered “will receive the consequences of.”
